{"completeness": 0.85, "citation_quality": 0.65, "severity_defensibility": 0.80, "overall_pass": false, "feedback": "The investigation demonstrates solid understanding of the attack mechanism and provides reasonable defensive recommendations, but has notable gaps in ATT&CK alignment and depth. Consider replacing T1212 and T1505.003 with T1083 (File and Directory Discovery) or T1526 (Enumerate External Targets), which better match the reconnaissance/discovery behavior. Additionally, the investigation could strengthen completeness by analyzing whether 192.0.2.150 is a known threat actor, checking for correlated alerts, and assessing the criticality of the /admin endpoint. The severity justification is solid and well-evidenced (blocked by WAF, no compromise), but add context on whether this endpoint typically faces probing to contextualize risk. {"completeness": 0.85, "citation_quality": 0.65, "severity_defensibility": 0.90, "overall_pass": false, "feedback": "The investigation demonstrates strong severity assessment and clear findings about the blocked attack, but has notable gaps in ATT&CK technique justification. T1190 is the most appropriate technique, but the analyst should have been more selective and explained why each technique applies to this specific attack chain. Additionally, the investigation could strengthen completeness by analyzing the attack pattern more deeply (e.g., whether this is reconnaissance, part of a scan campaign, or targeted) and by discussing compensating controls and detection gaps.
